newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet crisis ends, new ministers approved.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet crisis ends, new ministers approved.

text.p: Poland's two leftist ruling parties have signed an agreement ending their row over a share-out of powers, the coalition's smaller group said on Saturday.

Under the deal, clinched late on Friday, the Polish Peasant Party (PSL) will take over the key treasury ministry, to be set up on October 1 under a cabinet reform aimed at streamlining decision-making, PSL president Waldemar Pawlak said.

"We have agreed the PSL will present a candidate for the treasury minister, while the SLD (the Democratic Left Alliance) will control the ministry of administration and internal affairs and the economy ministry," Pawlak told a news conference.

He made clear Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko, a non-party technocrat and the author of the government economic policy, would keep his job. "The finance ministry is outside the sphere of the government reform," he said.

The agreement between the Peasant party and the ex-communist SLD ended a crisis in the three-year-old coalition, which erupted nearly four weeks ago when SLD's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz sacked a Peasant official from the cabinet without consultations.
The Peasants threatened to quit the coalition, which would have paved the way for early elections, otherwise not due until next year.

PSL's parliamentary speaker Jozef Zych said that having overcome the cabinet line-up dispute the coalition would focus on Poland's new constitution and bailing out debt-ridden health care and eduction systems.

Pawlak said Peasants' Planning Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz had been picked to take over the treasury ministry, the first of several portfolios to be created under the reform, which would also liquidate several ministries.

The treasury ministry will replace the privatisation portfolio, now headed by SLD's Wieslaw Kaczmarek -- one of the most liberal and pro-reform politicians in the ex-communists' group, despised by many Peasant deputies, who oppose selling off state assests.
Kaczmarek would be offered a senior position in the treasury ministry, Pawlak said, adding that details about his role would have to be further discussed.

SLD-linked President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who officialy appoints ministers, has made clear he would like Kaczmarek to keep the job and suggested PSL's Pietrewicz might lack the determination to pursue the much-needed privatisation.
"I highly value Mr Pietrewicz...but privatisation requires specific features of character, simply speaking courage," Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted Kwasniewski as saying on Friday.

Pietrewicz, a 55-year-old economics professor, has been in charge of macro-economic forecasts as the planning minister. Unless the coalition deal is broken Prime Minister Cimoszewicz is likely to ask the president on Monday to nominate him.
